name: Sierra
intro: Bret Taylor's customer-service agent company took seven quarters to reach its first $100 million of annualized revenue — then doubled it in two. Sierra hit roughly $200 million ARR in May 2026 at a $15.8 billion valuation. Here is the sourced timeline.

modelParagraphs: Sierra does not sell seats and mostly does not sell usage. It sells outcomes: customers pay per conversation the agent actually resolves. That aligns the vendor with the buyer's real metric — deflected tickets — and it makes contract value grow with support volume instead of headcount, which is exactly the wrong direction for a legacy per-agent license.

The catch is that outcome pricing only works with heavy implementation. Sierra bundles configuration and ongoing optimization into multi-year enterprise agreements, which is why the first $100 million took seven quarters and the second took two: the hard part is the first deployment in each account, and everything after that compounds.
revenueMix: Multi-year agreements with large support orgs.
Configuration and tuning bundled into the deal.
New channels and languages inside existing accounts.

faqs.a: Sierra reached roughly $200 million in annualized recurring revenue in May 2026, double the $100 million it reported in November 2025.

faqs.q: How Fast Did Sierra Reach $100M ARR?
faqs.a: About 21 months from its February 2024 public launch — seven quarters — then it doubled to $200 million in the following two quarters.

faqs.q: How Does Sierra Charge for Its AI Agents?
faqs.a: Primarily outcome-based pricing: customers pay per conversation the agent resolves, inside multi-year enterprise agreements that include implementation.
More than $15 billion — a $950 million Series E led by Tiger Global and GV in May 2026 priced the company at roughly $15.8 billion.

faqs.q: If an Agent Fails to Resolve a Ticket, Does the Customer Still Pay?
faqs.a: Under outcome pricing the billable event is a resolved conversation, so an escalation to a human is not what the customer is charged for. Exact definitions of resolution sit inside multi-year enterprise contracts and are not public.

ctaDescription: Agents priced per resolved conversation don't fit legacy billing. Clink meters outcomes, manages the plans and carries merchant-of-record tax for conversational products.
